scenario.label: Credit sales against this quarter target
scenario.brief: We are tracking the credit sales target for this quarter: 40 approved facilities and N120m disbursed across the team. I want to know for each person what is actually happening, not what activity they did: how many are in the pipeline, where each one is stuck, whether the follow-up happened, and what is stopping conversion. I want to be able to tell the difference between somebody who cannot deliver, somebody who is blocked, somebody who has not understood the target, and somebody whose progress is real but not yet visible.
scenario.theDecision: Femi is the one with a real capability problem (no conversion, activity high, has never asked for help). Ngozi is genuinely blocked by credit committee turnaround and her numbers are real. Kwame does not understand the target - he is counting applications, not approvals. The manager believes the team is behind because of the market. A right answer separates those four and does not average them into "the team is behind".

people.name: Bisi Adeyemi
people.remit: Sales manager. Owns the quarter target of 40 approved facilities and N120m disbursed.
people.truth: The team is at 11 approved and N31m against 40 and N120m, seven weeks into the quarter. She believes the problem is the market and the credit committee. She has not looked at the per-person numbers since week two. She approved every pipeline report without reading the detail. She has never had a conversation with Femi about conversion. She thinks Kwame is her strongest performer because his application count is the highest.
people.manner: Busy and confident. Talks about the team as one thing. Gives a number when asked for one.

people.name: Femi Okonkwo
people.remit: Relationship officer, Lagos mainland. Target 12 approved facilities this quarter.
people.truth: Two approved, N4m. He has visited 46 businesses and taken 31 applications. None of the 31 has been submitted to credit because he has not collected the bank statements and he does not push customers for documents. He has never told anybody this. When asked what is in the way he says the customers are slow. He has not asked Bisi for help. He works long hours and his visit numbers are the highest on the team.
people.manner: Eager and hardworking and talks in activity: visits, calls, forms. Deflects to the customer when asked about outcomes. Never says he needs help. If asked directly and plainly whether he has submitted anything, he admits it.

people.name: Ngozi Eze
people.remit: Relationship officer, Ikeja. Target 14 approved facilities this quarter.
people.truth: Six approved, N19m. Eleven complete files sitting at credit committee, the oldest submitted 34 days ago. She has chased the committee four times in writing and escalated once to the head of credit, who did not reply. If the eleven clear she is ahead of target. She is the only one on the team who has escalated anything.
people.manner: Precise and slightly impatient. Has dates and numbers ready. Names people and what she asked them for.

people.name: Kwame Mensah
people.remit: Relationship officer, Surulere. Target 14 approved facilities this quarter.
people.truth: Three approved, N8m. He reports 22 and believes he is ahead, because he is counting applications taken as sales. He has said "22" in every report. Nobody has corrected him. When the difference between an application and an approval is explained to him he understands it immediately and is embarrassed.
people.manner: Cheerful and confident. States his 22 as fact. Answers questions directly and honestly.

patterns.observationText: Work is described as tasks like 'pushing' and 'having conversations' without connecting them to the goal they are meant to achieve.
A delivery blockage is attributed entirely to an external party, with no next step owned to resolve it.
Coordination effort is described, but the blocker it is aimed at is not reducing.
Work is described in terms of an activity (having 22 applications in a pipeline) rather than the outcome the work is for (getting applications approved).
The same problem with the credit committee has been raised before and is reported again as unresolved.
A high level of communication with customers has not succeeded in removing the blockers to progress.
The reason for the lack of progress is attributed to external factors, without naming anything in the person's control to change the outcome.
The same problem was reported in previous periods and is still blocking all submissions.
The same external blocker is named again this period, with no progress reported in resolving it.
Confident statements about being "ahead of the game" are based on the number of submitted applications, not the approved ones that are the actual goal.
Confident reporting of team-level numbers sits beside a personal target that has not been met for more than one period.
A lot of communication is described, but the same blockers from the credit committee are still standing.
Failures are attributed to external factors like the market or the credit committee, without naming actions within the person's own control.
A promise to 'push' the credit committee was made before and is repeated, without the committee's delays being resolved.
The same misunderstanding of submitted versus approved applications was raised in a previous period and required intervention again to be resolved.
